lots.title: Stockport Town Centre School — Multi-Disciplinary Design Team Appointment
lots.description: Synthetic single-scope lot representing the undivided procurement. Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council (SMBC) is appointing an architecturally led multidisciplinary design and advisory team to deliver a new exemplar all-through (primary + secondary) town centre school on a brownfield site in Stockport town centre. The initial team composition to be procured is Architect, MEP, Structural and Civil Engineer, Principal Designer under the Building Safety Act 2022, and Principal Designer under CDM 2015; additional disciplines may be appointed by the Architect (in-house or externally procured) and reviewed at the end of each RIBA stage. The appointment is let via a Competitive Flexible Procedure with a Stage 1 competency submission narrowed to a maximum of three shortlisted suppliers, followed by a Stage 2 detailed submission including pricing and social value. The primary focus for RIBA Stage 2 is MEP and Structural Engineer involvement; RIBA Stage 2 funding is secured from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, and the procurement is written with the option to terminate or pause at each RIBA stage. Detailed scopes of service for each discipline are deferred to Appendix A (Scope of Services: Architectural, BR Principal Designer, CDM Principal Designer, MEP, Structures and Civils).
requirements: Deliver an architecturally led multi-disciplinary design team for a new town centre all-through school in Stockport, initially covering Architect, MEP, Structural/Civil Engineer, BR Principal Designer and CDM Principal Designer (Section 3.2).
Support the design from inception through the RIBA Plan of Work stages; primary focus at award is RIBA Stage 2 delivery with MEP and Structural Engineer involvement (Section 3.2).

Comply with RIBA Plan of Work, CDM 2015 Regulations, Building Safety Act 2022, Building Regulations (England and Wales), Building Regulations Approved Document B (Fire Safety), BS 9999, Environment Act 2021, Air Quality Standards Regulations 2010, Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, Equality Act 2010, and BS8300 inclusive design (Sections 3.6 and 7).
Comply with the Council's Climate Action Now and Social Value commitments (Section 3.6).
Deliver BIM Level 2 with COBie data as a mandatory information-management standard (Section 3.5).
Share project information via the SMBC SharePoint platform (Section 3.5).
Contribute to sustainable design outcomes including environmental performance, energy efficiency, materials selection and long-term operational impact (Section 7).

Meet Stage-2 performance KPIs monitored at Design Team Meetings: minimal design queries/changes during tender period, design meets client requirements, design meets budget requirement/limitations, attendance at required meetings, attendance at site visits, pro-active conduct (including email response within 3 working days and accurate snag/defect logging), and meeting Social Value commitments (Section 6, Performance Measures Table, all Pass/Fail).

Appointed personnel must hold the requisite qualifications, professional registration, accreditation and licensing — Architect: registered with ARB (preferably chartered RIBA) and/or MRICS/FRICS; MEP: CEng or IEng via Engineering Council UK or MCIBSE/FCIBSE or MIET or MIMechE; Structural & Civils: registered with ICE and IStructE (preferably chartered ICE/IStructE/CIOB); CDM Principal Designer: membership of a recognised body (RIBA, CIAT, ICE, IStructE), demonstrable knowledge of CDM 2015, SSIP accreditation (CHAS, SMAS or SafeContractor) and Professional Indemnity insurance; BR Principal Designer: competency standard PAS 8671:2022, delivered in-house or via specialist sub-consultant (Section 9, Skills and Expertise).

Stage 1 Competency Submission: provide a written response to the competency questions, scored on the published assessment scale (Unacceptable=0 through Outstanding=6); any quality question scored Unacceptable, Poor or Deficient results in full exclusion of the submission (Section 9 Stage 1 Competency Submission and scoring matrix).

Stage 2 submission (post-shortlisting) requires signing a confidentiality/non-disclosure agreement prior to receiving the detailed Stage 2 pack and will include numerous qualitative questions, a pricing schedule and social value commitments (Section 6 and Section 9 Stage 1 Competency Submission trailing paragraphs).

Scopes of service for each discipline are defined in Appendix A (Architectural Scope of Service, BR Principal Designer Scope of Service, CDM Principal Designer Scope of Service, MEP Scope of Service, Structures and Civils Scope of Service) — the Consultant shall cite and evidence all relevant qualifications, accreditations and licences; failure to do so may result in disqualification (Section 10 Annexes and Section 9 trailing paragraph).

evaluation_criteria.criterion: Stage 1 Competency Submission — qualitative scoring matrix
evaluation_criteria.summary: Stage 1 submissions are scored independently using a seven-point scale: Unacceptable (0), Poor (1), Deficient (2), Satisfactory (3), Good (4), Excellent (5), Outstanding (6). A score of Unacceptable, Poor or Deficient on any quality question results in the full exclusion of the submission. A maximum of three shortlisted suppliers will be progressed to Stage 2. Specific Stage 1 competency questions, their individual weightings, and the pass threshold are not enumerated in this document.
evaluation_criteria.weighting_text: Per-question scoring 0–6 on the published matrix; scores of 0–2 on any quality question cause full exclusion. Individual question weightings are not specified in this document.

evidence_anchor.anchor_text: Submissions will be scored independently, using the scoring matrix below. … Unacceptable 0 … Poor 1 … Deficient 2 … Satisfactory 3 … Good 4 … Excellent 5 … Outstanding 6 … This score for any quality question will result in the full exclusion of the submission.

evaluation_criteria.criterion: Stage 2 Detailed Submission — qualitative questions, pricing schedule and social value commitments
evaluation_criteria.summary: Stage 2 is described as a more detailed submission comprising numerous qualitative questions, a pricing schedule and social value commitments. Progression to Stage 2 is conditional on signing a confidentiality/non-disclosure agreement given the sensitivity of the project. Concrete Stage 2 weightings (quality/price/social value split), individual questions, and the pass/fail threshold are not published in this document and will be released if bidders reach Stage 2.
evaluation_criteria.weighting_text: Not fixed in this document; quality/price/social value weighting is deferred to the Stage 2 pack released to shortlisted bidders under NDA.

evidence_anchor.section_ref: Section 9 (second occurrence) — Stage 1 Competency Submission, trailing paragraphs
evidence_anchor.anchor_text: Stage two will involve a more detailed submission with numerous qualitative questions, pricing schedule and social value commitments. Further details of the scoring and additional information will be released if bidders reach the second stage, on the basis that a confidentiality agreement is signed.

evaluation_criteria.summary: Seven Pass/Fail post-award KPIs monitored at Design Team Meetings: (1a) minimal design queries/changes during tender period (target zero, excluding client-initiated changes); (2) design/report meets client requirements; (3) design meets budget requirement/limitations; (4) attendance at required meetings; (5) site attendance compliance; (6) pro-active conduct (3-working-day email response, early warnings, liaison, accurate snag/defect logging); (7) Social Value commitments met (added to pre-start and progress meeting agendas). These are contract-performance measures, not tender-evaluation criteria, but are included here because they materially shape Stage 2 scoring expectations.
evaluation_criteria.weighting_text: All seven measures are Pass/Fail; there are no numeric weightings. The KPIs are performance-monitoring measures applied post-award.

warnings.message: The procurement is a single-scope multi-disciplinary appointment and is not divided into lots. This skill emits a single synthetic lot (lot_number="1") covering the full Design Team scope so downstream persistence can attach lot-scoped evidence. The five disciplines referenced in the title (Architect, MEP, Structures & Civils, BR Principal Designer, CDM Principal Designer) are team-composition roles within the single appointment, not separate lots, consistent with the pre-existing notice-level lot metadata (single lot, contract reference 020417).

Section 5 states only 'The scope of services for the required disciplines are detailed within the Appendices' and Section 10 lists five Annex A entries (Architectural, BR Principal Designer, CDM Principal Designer, MEP, Structures and Civils scopes of service). The body of this document does not enumerate the per-discipline deliverables, activities, or per-RIBA-stage outputs — those live in the annex scope-of-service documents which are not embedded in this specification's Docling payload.

This procurement is for professional design/advisory services, not for physical goods. No SKU-like product requirements, quantities, or technical product attributes are itemised. product_requirement_seeds is emitted as an empty array. Downstream product-candidate generation will remain empty for this document; any future BoQ or equipment schedule produced during RIBA stages is out of scope for this specification.

No CPV (Common Procurement Vocabulary) codes are cited anywhere in the document body. The upstream notice carries an internal buyer category of '150000 - Consultancy' but that is a ProContract portal category, not a CPV code. cpv_codes on the lot is emitted empty per skill contract (authoritative truth from the tender document only).

Stage 2 evaluation criteria, individual question weightings, and the quality/price/social-value split are explicitly deferred — 'Further details of the scoring and additional information will be released if bidders reach the second stage, on the basis that a confidentiality agreement is signed.' The pre-existing notice_lots record (from the Briefing document) references an indicative Stage 2 split of 60% quality / 40% price / 20% social value but this specification does not itself publish those weights.

evidence_anchors.anchor_text: Document 2 Specification For: Stockport Town Centre School — Multi-Disciplinary Design Team (Architect, MEP, Structures & Civils, BR Principal Designer & CDM Principal Designer)

Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council (SMBC) is a unitary authority in Greater Manchester … Stockport Council are proposing to develop a new exemplar town centre school, within the heart of Stockport.

This procurement seeks to appoint an architecturally led multidisciplinary design and advisory team (initially including Architect, MEP, Structural and Civil Engineer, BR Principal Designer and CDM Principal Designer) to support the delivery of a new through school within the centre of Stockport.
It is anticipated that key information will be shared utilising SMBC SharePoint platform. BIM Level 2 with COBie data is a requirement.

RIBA Plan of Work and current Building Regulations. CDM 2015 Regulations and other statutory planning and heritage requirements. Building Safety Act 2022 … Building Regulations Approved Document B (Fire Safety) … BS 9999 … The Environment Act 2021 … The Air Quality Standards Regulations 2010 … Inclusive design principles and BS8300 (accessibility).

Stockport Council are commencing preliminary market engagement by issuing an Expression of Interest to suppliers through Stage 1 of the Competitive Flexible Procedure. This engagement will be conducted over 30 business days, with bidders providing a written response to competency questions prior to the formal release of the tender opportunity to a maximum of three shortlisted suppliers.
